items.title: K-flatness of a complex of modules is checked on stalks
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a ringed space X and a complex K of O_X-modules, the lemma shows that K is K-flat if and only if every stalk of K is K-flat over the corresponding local ring (statement lines 5872-5879). One direction is a stalkwise argument: tensor products and direct sums commute with taking stalks and exactness is checked on stalks, so exactness of the relevant total complexes follows from exactness of their stalks (proof lines 5882-5886). The converse is more substantial: given an acyclic complex M over the local ring at a point, its pushforward by the skyscraper functor is an acyclic complex of O_X-modules, so tensoring it with the K-flat K gives an acyclic total complex, and taking stalks at the point recovers the total complex of M with the stalk of K, which is therefore acyclic (proof lines 5887-5894). The claim is H2: one direction is bookkeeping with stalks, while the converse requires inventing the skyscraper pushforward to transfer acyclicity from the local ring to the space.
